documents.unit: Center for the Advancement of Teaching and Learning (CATL), Office of Education
documents.title: MUSC AI Acceptable Use Framework for Academic Tasks
documents.summary: CATL page presenting MUSC's five-category AI Acceptable Use Framework for Academic Tasks, which instructors apply task by task, with documentation expectations and faculty support tools. It calls itself a guiding framework rather than a policy and sits inside the Plagiarism and AI Guideline; the Honor Council handles integrity cases.
documents.stance_why: The page says "instructors will specify one of five categories of AI use for each task" and "Each faculty member is responsible for creating their own guidelines", so the university sets tiers but no default; stance is delegates.

units.why: The page says the framework is "not a policy statement" but a guiding framework; this defines the status of the guidance, an institution-level statement of nature, so P56 (no decision-maker is named, so not P04).
units.anchor: This is not a policy statement.
units.frag_start: This is not a policy statement.
units.frag_end: This is not a policy statement.

units.why: "AI tools should not replace the human connections, expertise, and critical reasoning" is an institutional principle framing all later rules. P56 chosen over P32 because it addresses the educational experience at large, not a student task.
units.anchor: AI tools should not replace the human connections, expertise, and critical reasoning
units.frag_start: we strongly believe that AI tools

units.why: MUSC "deliberately uses the term academic tasks rather than simply assignments or assessments", covering simulations, lab reports and research projects. It defines what the guidance covers, so P61.

units.why: "instructors will specify one of five categories" sorts uses into named levels, so P05 (the per-task decision by instructors is also P04, covered in the next unit).
units.anchor: instructors will specify one of five categories
units.frag_start: instructors will specify one of five categories
units.frag_end: of AI use for each task.
units.policy: Instructors specify one of five categories of AI use for each academic task.

units.why: "Instructors will designate which category applies to each task" places the decision per task with the instructor, so P04; P05 covers the categories themselves in another unit.
units.anchor: Instructors will designate which category applies
units.frag_start: Instructors will designate which category applies
units.policy: Instructors designate which category applies to each task based on learning objectives and assessment goals.

units.why: "Students must identify the specified category for each task and provide any documentation required" binds students to know the designation and document use. P24 chosen because the explicit duty is providing documentation; P10 fits less as no asking is stated.
units.anchor: Students must identify the specified category for each task
units.frag_start: Students must identify the specified category
units.policy: Students must identify the specified category for each task and provide any documentation required.

units.why: Category one: "AI may not be used at any point during the task". A ban on AI for the whole category of tasks; P01 (default ban) rather than P22 because the sentence is not limited to exams.
units.anchor: AI may not be used at any point during the task
units.frag_start: AI may not be used
units.policy: In Category 1 (No AI), AI may not be used at any point during the task.

units.why: "board style exams or clinical skills demonstrations fall into this category" assigns exams and in-person demonstrations to No AI; P22.
units.anchor: or clinical skills demonstrations fall into this category.
units.frag_start: or clinical skills demonstrations
units.policy: Board-style exams and clinical skills demonstrations fall into Category 1 (No AI).

units.why: "Any AI use here would undermine the intent to measure unassisted human performance" gives the reason for No AI, an assessment-validity rationale. P41 chosen over P33 since nothing shifts in weight.
units.anchor: Any AI use here would undermine the intent
units.frag_start: Any AI use here would undermine

units.why: Category two: "AI may only assist with high level brainstorming or outlining"; a narrow permitted use, brainstorming, so P15.
units.anchor: AI may only assist with high level brainstorming
units.frag_start: AI may only assist with
units.policy: In Category 2 (AI Planning), AI may only assist with high-level brainstorming or outlining, such as generating a draft structure for a paper.

units.why: "Final content must be, original" limits Category 2 work to student-created final content; P19 (AI may not produce the submitted work).
units.anchor: Final content must be, original.
units.frag_start: Final content must be, original.
units.policy: In Category 2 (AI Planning), final content must be original.

units.why: "Documentation may be required regarding prompts used" conditions Category 2 on documenting prompts; P25 (prompt details) rather than P24 because prompts are named.
units.anchor: Documentation may be required
units.frag_start: Documentation may be required
units.policy: In Category 2 (AI Planning), documentation may be required regarding prompts used and which AI suggestions were integrated.

units.why: Category three allows AI "in a limited way to complete only specific aspects of the task", such as formatting and grammar. Narrow allowed uses; P18 fits the listed formatting and grammar examples.
units.anchor: AI may be used in a limited way
units.frag_start: AI may be used in a limited way
units.policy: In Category 3 (AI Limited), AI may be used in a limited way to complete only specific aspects of the task, such as formatting data tables, creating visual layouts, or checking grammar and spelling.

units.why: "all core work must be completed without AI assistance" bars AI from the substance of the task in Category 3; P19.
units.anchor: all core work must be completed
units.frag_start: all core work must be completed
units.policy: In Category 3 (AI Limited), all core work must be completed without AI assistance.

units.why: "Documentation may be required regarding each AI interaction and how outputs were evaluated" asks for per-interaction records and evaluation; P26 over P24 because of the logs and evaluation reflection.
units.anchor: Documentation may be required regarding each AI interaction
units.frag_start: Documentation may be required regarding
units.policy: In Category 3 (AI Limited), documentation may be required regarding each AI interaction and how outputs were evaluated.

units.why: Category four: "AI may be used extensively to complete any element of the task as directed by the course instructor"; broad permission, P02.
units.anchor: AI may be used extensively
units.frag_start: AI may be used extensively
units.policy: In Category 4 (AI Extensive), AI may be used extensively to complete any element of the task as directed by the course instructor.

units.why: The Category 4 example, "verifying, critiquing, and correcting AI generated summaries for accuracy, bias and completeness", has students check AI output; P31.
units.anchor: and correcting AI generated summaries for accuracy,
units.frag_start: and correcting AI generated summaries
units.policy: In the Category 4 example of a literature review with AI, students verify, critique, and correct AI-generated summaries for accuracy, bias and completeness.

units.why: "Documentation may be required regarding decision points, corrections made, and rationale for accepting or rejecting AI generated content" asks for reflective records in Category 4; P26.
units.anchor: Documentation may be required regarding decision points,
units.frag_start: Documentation may be required regarding decision points,
units.policy: In Category 4 (AI Extensive), documentation may be required regarding decision points, corrections made, and rationale for accepting or rejecting AI-generated content.

units.why: Category five: "AI is required to complete the task", with analysis of strengths and limitations "expected". AI is built into the work, so unit_stance require; nearest type is P02 (expects AI use), as no type covers requirement more closely.
units.anchor: AI is required to complete the task
units.frag_start: AI is required to complete the task
units.policy: In Category 5 (AI Exploration), AI is required to complete the task and serves as both a subject of inquiry and an innovation catalyst; critical analysis and thorough examination of AI strengths and limitations are expected.

units.why: Category 5 states "documentation may be required regarding the research process, analytic methods, and evaluation of AI's impact"; process documentation, P26.
units.anchor: documentation may be required
units.frag_start: of AI in patient care, documentation may be required
units.policy: In Category 5 (AI Exploration), documentation may be required regarding the research process, analytic methods, and evaluation of AI's impact.

units.why: The video says AI "cannot replace the personalized expertise, mentorship, and critical thinking that define MUSC"; a principle that AI must not replace human thinking, P32.

units.why: CATL provides "Ready-to-use syllabus language" and "Brightspace icons for AI use designations" so faculty can clearly communicate expectations; P09 (syllabus/assignment language) rather than P63.
units.anchor: Ready-to-use syllabus language

units.policy: CATL provides ready-to-use syllabus language, assignment language aligned with the framework, student communication resources, Brightspace icons for AI use designations, and implementation guidance.

units.anchor: practical tools, resources, and consultation services
units.frag_start: we have developed practical tools, resources, and consultation services
units.policy: CATL provides practical tools, resources, and consultation services to help educators make learning outcome-based decisions about AI integration and communicate clear expectations.

units.why: Faculty are "encouraged to design assignments around learning outcomes" rather than "AI avoidance"; assignment redesign, P35.
units.anchor: Rather than designing assignments around AI avoidance
units.frag_start: Rather than designing assignments around AI avoidance
units.policy: Faculty are encouraged to design assignments around learning outcomes, authentic demonstration of learning, and the professional competencies students must ultimately develop, rather than around AI avoidance.

units.policy: Educators define observable evidence of authentic student reasoning, asking what thinking or judgment must be made visible to grade.

units.policy: Educators select the appropriate designation (No AI, AI Planning, AI Limited, AI Extensive, or AI Exploration), explain their decision to students and communicate expectations clearly.
